when matias stepped out from the metro platform walking west on pressler when she struck matias [medical facility] via ambulance by hfd. the reporting officer then issued watkins a citation (100226) for driving without a license and then instructed watkins to have a driver with a valid license come to the location and pick up the vehicle which she did. the reporting officer then collected all necessary [medical facility] to have a follow interview with the matias [medical facility] he was provided with a phone for a foreign translator to communicate with matias effectively. matias told the translator that he had the right of way in the crosswalk and the driver of unit 1 was speeding. the reporting office then cleared the scene at approximately 0824 hours.

records.public_safe_text: unit #1 was traveling north in the parking lot of [roadway]. the pedestrian was traveling west, with multiple shopping carts. the pedestrian had entered into the intersection, just in front of the store. according to pedestrian and witness, robert harper (281)739-2179, unit #1 struck its front right corner to the string of shopping carts, causing the carts to fall over and the pedestrian to fall onto the pavement. witness said the vehicle pulled away from the crash and the driver got out and checked his vehicle for damage. the driver of unit #1 then drove north through the parking lot. raymond perry, off-duty wichita falls police officer, approached the scene as unit #1 was driving away. perry took a photo of the fleeing vehicle and tag. pedestrian said he felt pain in his back, [medical facility] for medical attention. after a records check was conducted the vehicle was located at the registered owners home. i spoke with brian w. westmoreland. brian admitted he was driving unit #1. brian said he believed the pedestrian struck the right back quarter panel of his vehicle with the carts. brian said he got out to check for damage, but he needed to be somewhere, so he left the scene. it should be noted, brian had parked his vehicle in his driveway, and partially under a carport. brian pointed out damage to the right rear quarter panel. i had to squeeze between unit #1 and another vehicle to observe damage to the front right corner. i took photographs of the damage. i received a photograph from security video of the parking lot, from walmart loss prevention officer. from the photograph i received it appeared unit #1's front right corner was striking the carts. the photograph was placed in the wfpd property room, as evidence.

records.deidentified_narrative: police responded to the listed location for a call for a crash where unit 1 allegedly struck ped 1. ped 1 reported unit 1 had backed up into her while she was walking in the front of the location near the driveway ped 1 initially stated she was not hurt and did not require ems but later on during the incident she stated her back hurt. despite this, ped 1 still refused ems. ped 1 stated the driver of unit 1 was at the location and i went to contact him. the driver of unit 1 stated he was backing up into the driveway of the listed incident location when he heard an employee at the property shout at him. this caused driver 1 to stop unit 1 suddenly, and he heard a loud thud on the back of unit 1. ped 1 then walked up to driver 1, pounding on the windows of unit 1 to get driver 1's attention. driver 1 stated he attempted to speak with ped 1 but ped 1 seemed to be agitated at the situation so driver 1 moved further into the parking lot to wait for police. a witness on scene stated he observed unit 1 backing up into the parking lot from the entrance of the location and he observed ped 1 walking behind it looking at her phone, seemingly not paying attention. the witness stated he shouted out to driver 1 who immediately stopped but ped 1 was observed slapping the back of unit 1. driver 1 stated he couldn't see behind him too well due to how dark the area around him was and through my observations the entrance of the parking lot did appear to be rather dark with no ambient lighting to be seen. i observed unit 1 and saw that there was a handprint on the back of the vehicle, seemingly from ped 1 from where she slapped unit 1. no damage was observed on unit 1 or claimed. ped 1 had no observable injuries on her that made it obvious she was struck by a vehicle. based on the statements made by ped 1, driver 1 i determined that a crash may not have actually occurred as ped 1 seems to have struck unit 1 with her hand when it stopped as opposed to unit 1 striking her. however, due to ped 1's claims of a crash and possible injury, this report was written. both driver 1 and ped 1 received the [case id] and were instructed on what to do next. while on patrol, i was contacted by a family member of ped 1 [medical facility] after all and requested further information regarding the crash and what to do next. this was requested of me through the service agent at the north substation through [roadway] to ped 1's residence and provide her with the information directly as opposed to calling the family member. i contacted ped 1's family member while ped 1 was sitting in a chair at the [medical facility] to get ped 1 treated, i was able to provide them with further information on how to follow-up. this was done under sapd-2019-0191541. no further action was taken. coban and bwc is available for both incidents.

witness on scene stated he observed unit 1 backing up into the parking lot from the entrance of the location and he observed ped 1 walking behind it looking at her phone, seemingly not paying attention. the witness stated he shouted out to driver 1 who immediately stopped but ped 1 was observed slapping the back of unit 1. driver 1 stated he couldn't see behind him too well due to how dark the area around him was and through my observations the entrance of the parking lot did appear to be rather dark with no ambient lighting to be seen. i observed unit 1 and saw that there was a handprint on the back of the vehicle, seemingly from ped 1 from where she slapped unit 1. no damage was observed on unit 1 or claimed. ped 1 had no observable injuries on her that made it obvious she was struck by a vehicle. based on the statements made by ped 1, driver 1 i determined that a crash may not have actually occurred as ped 1 seems to have struck unit 1 with her hand when it stopped as opposed to unit 1 striking her. however, due to ped 1's claims of a crash and possible injury, this report was written. both driver 1 and ped 1 received the [case id] and were instructed on what to do next. while on patrol, i was contacted by a family member of ped 1 [medical facility] after all and requested further information regarding the crash and what to do next. this was requested of me through the service agent at the north substation through [roadway] to ped 1's residence and provide her with the information directly as opposed to calling the family member. i contacted ped 1's family member while ped 1 was sitting in a chair at the [medical facility] to get ped 1 treated, i was able to provide them with further information on how to follow-up. this was done under sapd-2019-0191541. no further action was taken. coban and bwc is available for both incidents.

records.deidentified_narrative: on february 11, 2019, at approximately 1:54 a. m., s/sgt. s. wesley #937 and police responded to a [roadway] at westbound i-30, just east of the dolphin exit. we arrived on scene at 1:57 a. m. and dallas fire department, engine #32, driven by lt. sideres [identifier] and dallas fire & rescue truck #32, was positioned and blocking off the freeway, which prevented any oncoming traffic from entering the accident area. once on scene, we encountered a pedestrian, lying in the roadway, across several portions of the freeway, between ferguson and dolphin. the pedestrian was confirmed to be deceased at 2:04 a. m., by lt. sideres (dallas fire department). the driver who struck the pedestrian and witnesses stated that after the pedestrian was initially hit, he was again struck by a 18 wheeler, that fled the scene. the driver who initially struck the pedestrian was identified by texas identification card as gomez, leonel, w/m, december 23, 1992. gomez was driving a white honda accord, texas license plate# [identifier]. gomez stated that he was traveling westbound i-30, [roadway], just west of ferguson, when the pedestrian was running north across the freeway. gomez attempted to brake, to avoid hitting the pedestrian, but was unsuccessful. gomez struck the pedestrian with the front left, causing damage to the vehicle, causing the pedestrian to be thrown approximately fifty-feet. witness #1 was driving in the same direction, observed the accident and swerved, to avoid from hitting the pedestrian in the roadway. in the process of the first witness swerving, he was able to avoid hitting the pedestrian, but ended up hitting the concrete barriers (zipper walls) instead. this accident was worked separately, as a minor accident by deputy b. riser #1159, under [case id]. witness #2 was driving, also in the same direction and observed the accident. the second witness attempted to [roadway] to shield the pedestrian from being hit by any other approaching vehicles. as the second witness was positioning her car, a 18-wheeler drove past her, striking the pedestrian once again, in the process. the driver of the 18-wheeler is unknown, and no description for the 18-wheeler was available, due to the driver not stopping, after striking the pedestrian. after driving over the pedestrian, the 18-wheeler left the body of the pedestrian dismantled and spread out across all four lanes and over several areas, which covered several hundred feet of the freeway, between ferguson and dolphin. the medical examiner was requested at 2:47 a. m. the driver and both witnesses completed affidavits, which were turned in to detective embry #521, with the dallas sheriff's department vehicle crimes unit (vcu). lt. cavnor #14153 (fire engine #783), d. g. reeves [identifier] and brandy carr (fire truck #32), from dallas fire & rescue arrived to the scene at 3:15 a. m.. they were there to see if the driver who struck the pedestrian or the first witness, who hit the zipper walls, needed medical attention. all who were seen by dallas fire & rescue, declined to be transported or further evaluated by medical personnel. protech/hazmat was requested by lt. cavnor from dallas fire & rescue at 2:48 a. m. to clean the contamination from the scene. the dallas county medical examiner, trina #939, arrived on scene at 3:30 a. m. to collect the deceased pedestrian’s remains. chubbs towing arrived on scene at 4:34 a. m. and cleared at 5:54 a. m., transporting the white honda accord to walnut hill towing facility. a hold, for the vehicle crimes unit was placed on the white, honda accord. protech arrived on scene at 4:58 a. m. the scene was completely cleared at 6:04 a. m. and all lanes were re-opened for normal usage and operations.*****times fixed per fmr [date] [identifier]
